question: Do the similarly named Palanas water features in the 1998 fish-survey abstract, the historical Lemery fisheries order, and the Naic/Timalan monitoring bulletin refer to one physical watercourse?

sourceFindings.evidence: The NAST proceedings abstract reports a 1998 survey at one Palanas River site and describes that study feature as a diverging branch of Pansipit with a separate outlet to Balayan Bay about 3 km from the Pansipit mouth.
sourceFindings.limits: One-page abstract only; it supplies no coordinates, municipality for the Palanas site, route, map, species list or station records.

sourceFindings.evidence: The BFAR-hosted historical Fisheries Administrative Order names Palanas Creek within Lemery, Batangas, and describes tidal waters and tributaries extending to a junction with Pansipit River.
sourceFindings.limits: Historical scanned order with imperfect OCR. The named creek may or may not be the same feature as the 1998 Palanas River site. This review does not treat the order as current fishing law, access permission, or a present-day route definition.

sourceFindings.evidence: The indexed text of the official DENR-EMB CALABARZON quarterly bulletin names Palanas River (Naic) among tributaries of Timalan River and places Timalan in Naic and Tanza, Cavite.
sourceFindings.limits: Direct PDF retrieval returned HTTP 403; only the official indexed excerpt was reviewed. It supplies no Palanas channel geometry or fish survey. Its 2006 water-classification context is not adopted as a current legal classification.

sourceFindings.evidence: The official Geoportal Data Inventory lists Water Body 1:10,000 and Water Body 1:50,000 as uploaded with metadata and Open under Memorandum Order No. 008, series of 2022; the inventory also says downloads are temporarily disabled for updating. On 2026-10-31 the public GeoServer WMS GetCapabilities endpoint returned HTTP 200 and advertised geoportal:waterbody10k and geoportal:waterbody50k as queryable, with CRS EPSG:4683 and CRS:84 and extents covering Cavite.
sourceFindings.limits: This is catalog/service availability evidence, not proof of a Palanas River feature or route. FeatureInfo probes returned empty collections at a secondary locator and a Taal control, so the identification result is indeterminate. The unauthenticated WFS capabilities endpoint returned HTTP 401. No vector features or geometry were retrieved or retained.

sourceFindings.evidence: The secondary page lists Tatlong Balon River and “Palanas River” as an alternative name and gives an approximate point at 14.35 N, 120.78333 E; that point was used only for a Geoportal WMS FeatureInfo probe.
sourceFindings.limits: The page is not an official source and does not establish that this feature is the same as the 2006 EMB Palanas River (Naic), the 1998 Pansipit/Balayan Bay study feature, or the historical Lemery Palanas Creek. The WMS probe returned no feature; no geometry or identity was adopted.

pansipitStudyFeature.decision: Keep the 1998 NAST study lead separate from both the Naic/Timalan tributary lead and the 1947 Palanas Creek name until a modern hydrography/LGU crosswalk resolves the relationship.

naicTimalanTributary.decision: Record as a distinct Cavite research lead because the 2006 bulletin explicitly supplies Naic and Timalan drainage context; do not transfer the historical Batangas fish richness to it.

historicalLemeryCreek.decision: Retain as a comparison source for the Batangas study lead, not as proof of present route, legal status or identity with the Naic feature.

nextActions: Seek current official Geoportal/NAMRIA or LGU feature-level metadata/data that identifies the Palanas River (Naic) channel and its Timalan connection. The catalog marks 1:10,000/1:50,000 water-body layers Open but downloads temporarily disabled; live WMS feature-info did not resolve a feature, so neither the catalog nor empty point probes can substitute for an official crosswalk.

Seek an official Lemery/Batangas river or cadastral crosswalk to determine whether the 1947 Palanas Creek and 1998 study Palanas River are related; preserve the historical source-era wording and do not rely on the order for current fishing rules.
For the 1998 Palanas fish aggregate, locate an independently licensed, site-resolved species source or written reuse permission before transcribing taxa.

inventory.catalogStatus: Both Water Body 1:10,000 and Water Body 1:50,000 are listed as Uploaded with metadata Yes and restriction Open under Memorandum Order No. 008, series of 2022; downloads are marked temporarily disabled for updating.
inventory.interpretation: Catalog snapshot only; does not identify the Palanas feature or guarantee that the live vector is currently downloadable.
